raw_response.rationale: This 2019 West Virginia University PhD dissertation conducts inferential econometric analyses across three essays, none of which estimates a SWiM-eligible legal/institutional rule-type effect on a Criterion 4 household or community water/sanitation service access outcome: (1) Essay 1 (PDF pp. 17-68, complete with Tables 2.3-2.4) estimates panel and Spatial Durbin models (N = 576, 48 states, 2000-2011) of the share of population served by public water systems incurring SDWA health-based violations on state per capita Personal Health Care expenditures, failing Criterion 4 because the outcome is aggregate medical spending rather than water/sanitation service access. (2) Essay 2 (PDF pp. 70-105) estimates hedonic OLS, spatial lag, and spatial quantile regressions (N = 1,985 single-family sales in Marion County, WV, 2012-2017) of prior-year Boil Water Notices (80% caused by pipe breaks/leaks) on log house sale prices ln(P) and derived marginal willingness to pay (MWTP), failing Criterion 2 (operational unreliability rather than a rule-type legal/tariff/governance intervention) and Criterion 4 (property prices / WTP only). (3) Essay 3 is truncated in the provided prompt text after PDF p. 105 (PDF pp. 106-180 omitted), but the Dissertation Abstract (PDF p. 4), Section 1.1.3 (PDF pp. 12-13), Table of Contents (PDF p. 7), and List of Tables (PDF p. 9) establish that it runs a cross-sectional OLS regression across 110 West Virginia Public Service Districts (Table 4.5) of residential water charges per 4,500 gallons on physical raw water supply source types (surface water, purchased water, multiple sources, NRCS flood-control impoundments) plus utility cost/scope controls (joint water-sewer service, debt, network length) to value raw water; WV Senate Bill 373 is discussed only as statewide policy context rather than a tested exposure. Confidence is set to medium solely because Essay 3's regression table (Table 4.5, p. 165 / PDF p. 174) lies in the truncated tail of the 180-page PDF.
